regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Kirkwood leads with 28" over the window, 13" on Friday. A Winter Storm Warning runs Friday through Saturday with gusty southwest wind. Sugar Bowl gets 27" and Palisades 26", with the biggest day Tuesday at 11".

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mammoth expects 13" total, with 8" on Friday. Heavy snow and very strong southwest wind, gusts to 85 mph, are the main concern. A Winter Storm Warning runs Friday through Saturday. The NWS is calling for more, 18" to 30" from Friday through Monday night.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler is forecast for 16" total, with 6" on Saturday. Most of the period brings rain and showers, and snow levels will matter more than totals. Cypress Mountain sees 5", with 4" on Sunday, under mostly rain.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: Powder Mountain leads with 10" total, 6" of it on Tuesday, when rain and snow is likely. Snowbasin is at 9" and Alta at 8". Expect mixed precipitation Tuesday and Saturday's snow in the mid-elevations.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Stevens Pass forecasts 8" total, with 4" on Sunday, but much of the period is rain and snow. Mt. Bachelor sees 7", with strong southwest wind Friday gusting to 52 mph. The NWS is calling for more, 6" to 11" from Friday through Monday night. Crystal Mountain sits at 7".

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Telluride forecasts 8" total, with 4" on Saturday, and the NWS is calling for more, 7" to 14" from Friday night through Tuesday night. Crested Butte expects 4" and Aspen Highlands 3", with light snow showers only.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Sun Valley forecasts 8" total, with 5" on Tuesday. Expect rain and snow mixes through Monday. Grand Targhee and Jackson Hole each see 2" on Tuesday, with snow showers likely.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Wolf Creek forecasts 8" total, with 4" on Saturday, and the NWS is calling for more, 16" to 28" from Friday night through Tuesday night. Taos sees 2" on Saturday, with snow showers and a slight chance of thunderstorms.

ahead.text: A storm is expected to bring widespread snow to the Sierra around Friday Nov 20, with the Climate Prediction Center reporting high uncertainty in its own forecast. The Salt Lake City NWS office says run-to-run consistency has been lacking.
